promise: Close the Guantánamo Bay detention camp within one year
description: Obama signed Executive Order 13492 on January 22, 2009, directing closure within one year. The detention facility remained in use after January 22, 2010.
evidence: Executive Order 13492 set a one-year deadline.
TIME reported in January 2015 that detention facilities remained in use.

promise: Pass comprehensive health care reform legislation in 2009
description: In a joint session address Obama told Congress reform 'must happen this year.' The Affordable Care Act was not signed until March 23, 2010, several months after the promised timeline.
evidence: ACA signed 2010-03-23, not in 2009
Reform did ultimately pass, fulfilling the substance of the promise

review.note: March 23, 2010 signing supported. September 9 attribution of 'must happen this year' and the exact year-end deadline need the speech. If confirmed, kept (delayed) is more consistent than partial.

role: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom
promise: Cut annual net migration to 'tens of thousands' by the end of the parliament
description: Cameron pledged to reduce net migration to under 100,000 during the 2010-2015 parliament. Net migration instead rose to about 298,000 in 2014 and 336,000 in the year to June 2015 — his office later said the target was 'not achieved.'
evidence: Net migration reached 336,000 by mid-2015
Cameron's own government admitted the target was not met

review.note: Goal and failure supported. May 13 announcement date unestablished; policy predates election. 298,000 refers to year ending September 2014; later migration estimates were revised.

role: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom
promise: Leave the European Union on 31 October 2019, 'do or die'
description: In his first speech as PM Johnson pledged the UK would leave the EU on October 31 'no ifs or buts.' Parliament forced a delay and Brexit occurred on January 31, 2020 — three months late but achieved.
evidence: UK left the EU on 2020-01-31
October 31 deadline missed after Parliament refused to ratify the deal

review.note: July 24 speech says 'no ifs or buts', not the different 'do or die' quotation. October deadline abandonment supported; need primary departure record and original quote date before replacing partial with kept (delayed).

role: UK Secretary of State for Health and Social Care
promise: Reach 100,000 coronavirus tests per day by the end of April 2020
description: Hancock announced the target on April 2. The April 30 total included mailed kits, not just processed tests.
evidence: Health Service Journal reported that the government's total included mailed kits.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the original completed-test metric cannot be reconciled to the reported count from the checked coverage.

role: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom
promise: Halve inflation during 2023
description: Sunak pledged in January 2023 to halve inflation during the year. The latest published rate was 10.7% for November 2022, below the October peak of 11.1%. CPI reached 4.6% in October 2023.
evidence: The government announced fulfillment on November 15, 2023 after October inflation fell to 4.6%.

role: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom
promise: 'Stop the boats' — end illegal small boat Channel crossings in 2023
description: Sunak made 'stop the boats' one of his five 2023 priorities and introduced the Illegal Migration Act to deliver it. 29,437 people crossed the Channel in small boats in 2023 — the second highest annual figure on record — and Sunak later admitted there was no 'firm date' for stopping crossings.
evidence: 29,437 arrivals in 2023, down only a third from 2022's record 45,755
Sunak admitted no firm target date in December 2023

review.note: Conflates a pledge to legislate with a guarantee of no crossings in 2023. No firm deadline was given; December 31 cannot be treated as the original deadline. Arrival count/ranking need Home Office series.

promise: The 2011 Atomic Energy Act amendment scheduled the last nuclear shutdowns for the end of 2022.
description: Germany's 2011 legislation set December 31, 2022 as the final nuclear shutdown deadline. Temporary legislation extended the last three plants until April 15, 2023, when they shut down.
evidence: Federal ministry records confirm final shutdown on April 15, 2023.

promise: Reduce unemployment to 7% by 2022
description: Macron's 2017 programme targeted unemployment of 7% by 2022, not 5%.
evidence: Contemporaneous March 2017 reporting identifies a 7% target.

review.note: 2017 target was 7%, not 5%; full employment belongs to the later term. May 7 is election day, not a sourced announcement. Reassess status against actual target and INSEE, not the false 5% threshold.

promise: Macron aimed to rebuild Notre-Dame within five years.
description: The cathedral was still undergoing restoration in April 2024 and reopened with ceremonies in December 2024, after the five-year target.
evidence: Contemporary April 2024 coverage described restoration as nearly complete.
The cathedral records December 7-8 reopening ceremonies.

promise: Repeal and replace Obamacare 'very quickly' in 2017
description: Trump repeatedly promised the Affordable Care Act would be repealed and replaced 'very quickly' after taking office. The Senate repeal effort collapsed on July 28, 2017 with John McCain's decisive vote, and the ACA remained law.
evidence: Senate rejected repeal 2017-07-28
ACA remains in force through 2026

review.note: July 28 repeal defeat supported. January 20 attribution and December 31 deadline for 'very quickly' need contemporaneous promise source. Through-2026 legal assertion not checked.

promise: Trump set a goal of having a COVID-19 vaccine available by the end of 2020, if possible.
description: Trump announced the qualified goal on May 15, 2020. FDA authorized emergency use of the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine in December 2020, within the target year.
evidence: The May 15 transcript makes the goal conditional.
FDA's December 2020 notice establishes emergency authorization, not unrestricted approval.

promise: End the Russia-Ukraine war within 24 hours of becoming president
description: Trump made a 24-hour peace claim during his campaign. On January 7, 2025 he discussed a six-month timeframe instead. Fighting continued after inauguration.
evidence: January 7 reporting describes a six-month hope.
AP reported after inauguration that the war continued.

review.note: January 7 remarks discussed six months, not a renewed 24-hour pledge. Earlier campaign pledge/failure supported, but replacement original date needs sourcing.

promise: End inflation within the first year of his second term
description: In an August 2024 economic address Trump pledged to use 'every tool' to defeat inflation within the first year of a second term. US CPI inflation remained positive at roughly 2.5-3% through 2025, and prices never fell.
evidence: CPI remained around 2.5-3% throughout 2025
Trump later said lowering prices was 'hard' and 'can't guarantee anything'

review.note: Senate report cites August 14 speech but first-year deadline unestablished. Ending inflation does not require prices to fall; current evidence conflates disinflation and deflation. Need speech and BLS series.

promise: Deliver 100 million COVID-19 vaccine doses in the first 100 days
description: Biden announced the 100-million-shot goal on December 8, 2020. His administration reported reaching it on March 19, 2021, ahead of the deadline, before increasing the target to 200 million.
evidence: March 25 transcript says the original goal was reached by day 58.
March 19 reporting confirms the 100-million milestone.

review.note: 100 million reached March 19, day 58, not April 21/day 92 (later 200-million milestone). Normalize first-100-days due date convention separately.

promise: Have 70% of American adults at least partly vaccinated by July 4, 2021
description: Biden's adult vaccination target was not reached by July 4, 2021.
evidence: The May 4 White House fact sheet sets the 70% adult first-dose goal and July 4 deadline.
Contemporary July 4 reporting records the shortfall.

promise: Withdraw all US troops from Afghanistan by September 11, 2021
description: Biden announced the withdrawal on April 14, 2021. CENTCOM reported completion in August, before the September 11 target.
evidence: The Defense Department records the April 14 announcement.
CENTCOM's completion account places withdrawal before the promised September deadline.

promise: Lift all rural poor out of poverty by 2020
description: Xi promised at the 19th Party Congress that China would eradicate poverty by 2020. The government declared success on February 25, 2021, saying 98.99 million rural residents had been lifted out of poverty. World Bank data broadly supports a dramatic reduction, though the official 'zero poverty' figure is contested.
evidence: Official declaration of poverty elimination 2021-02-25
World Bank data confirms extreme poverty fell to under 1% under China's standard

review.note: Retrieved World Bank methodological material distinguishes national from international poverty thresholds but does not establish this announcement date, 98.99 million figure or the asserted under-1% statistic. Official declaration is not independent verification of universal elimination.

promise: Aim to peak CO2 emissions before 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality before 2060
description: Xi announced these goals at the UN General Assembly on September 22, 2020. The pledge sets latest thresholds, not a prohibition on peaking earlier.
evidence: China's NDC records the September 22, 2020 announcement and both before-year targets.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: both target horizons remain future; the checked announcement and NDC establish the goals, not completion.

person: World Health Organization and United Nations
promise: Reach 70% COVID-19 vaccination coverage in every country by mid-2022.
description: The joint October 7, 2021 strategy set a country-by-country vaccination target. WHO reported in July 2022 that average country coverage was about 60%, so the universal 70% goal was not achieved despite substantial progress.
evidence: The October 7 strategy establishes the target and date.
WHO's July 22, 2022 update reports average country coverage of about 60%, below the universal 70% objective.

role: International agreement signatories (Copenhagen Accord / Paris Agreement)
promise: Mobilise $100 billion per year in climate finance for developing countries by 2020
description: Developed countries pledged to mobilise $100 billion annually for developing countries by 2020. OECD reports $83.3 billion in 2020, $89.6 billion in 2021 and $115.9 billion in 2022, the first year exceeding the target.
evidence: OECD identifies first fulfillment in 2022, two years after the original target.

review.note: OECD confirms 83.3 billion in 2020 and first reaching target in 2022. Developed countries, not all UNFCCC parties, were the financing providers. Exact Copenhagen adoption date needs agreement text. Annual ongoing obligation should not be collapsed into permanently kept status.

promise: Halve the proportion of people living in extreme poverty between 1990 and 2015
description: The MDG target was to halve the extreme-poverty proportion between 1990 and 2015. The UN's 2015 report said the target was achieved and estimated the developing-world rate fell from 47% to 14%.
evidence: UN 2015 report gives 47% and 14% for developing regions, using its then-current $1.25-a-day measure.
sources: United Nations Millennium Development Goals Report

review.note: 47% to 14% refers to developing regions, not global population. Goal success supported by UN report; exact September 8 adoption and 189 signatories require declaration.

promise: Musk forecast a fully autonomous Tesla demonstration from Los Angeles to New York by the end of 2017.
description: Musk forecast an autonomous coast-to-coast Tesla demonstration by the end of 2017. In February 2018 he acknowledged missing that target.
evidence: The dated TED interview establishes the original end-2017 target.
In Tesla's February 7, 2018 earnings call, Musk acknowledged the missed demonstration target. This assessment concerns that deadline, not all later autonomous-driving capability.
sources: Tesla earnings call via ROIC AI

promise: One million Tesla robotaxis on the road by 2020
description: At Autonomy Day Musk said Tesla would launch a robotaxi network and that there would be one million robotaxis on the road in 2020. No Tesla robotaxi service existed by the deadline, and even a limited robotaxi launch only arrived in pilot form in 2025.
evidence: Zero robotaxis deployed by end of 2020
Autonomous ride-hail pilots did not start until 2025

review.note: Search returned secondary prediction trackers pointing to contemporaneous CNBC reporting. Do not use the tracker alone to certify the quote, April 22 timing, zero deployments and 2025 launch history; linked original report needs checking.

promise: Produce 5,000 Model 3 cars per week by the end of 2017
description: Tesla reached a production rate of approximately 5,000 Model 3 vehicles per week in 2018, after its stated 2017 target.
evidence: Tesla's second-quarter 2018 report says approximately 5,000 Model 3s were produced in multiple July weeks.

review.note: Tesla filing supports achieving roughly 5,000/week in 2018, including multiple July weeks. May 3 2017 original forecast still needs original letter. 'Overnight shutdown push' unsupported; outcome was delayed achievement rather than partial production rate.

promise: Begin Cybertruck deliveries in late 2021
description: Cybertruck production was initially planned for late 2021. First deliveries took place November 30, 2023.
evidence: Deliveries occurred after the original target.

review.note: First deliveries were late. Unveiling date is local US time; verify November 22 UTC before changing date_promised.

promise: See the last case of polio within six years (by ~2018)
description: At the 2012 Rotary International Convention, Gates said that if everything went right, the world would see the last case of polio 'within the next six years.' Wild polio cases fell sharply but persisted in Pakistan and Afghanistan, and circulating vaccine-derived polio outbreaks continued globally past the deadline and into 2026.
evidence: Wild polio never reached zero; still endemic in 2026
Gates Foundation and GPEI kept extending the eradication timeline

review.note: No matching May 7, 2012 Rotary speech or six-year quotation located. Results instead describe a 2013 six-year eradication plan and a 2019 speech. Do not invent a promise date or treat this negative search as disproof.

promise: Zuckerberg said Facebook was expanding safety and security staffing from 10,000 to 20,000 during 2018.
description: Zuckerberg reiterated the safety and security staffing target in September 2018. Facebook's December 4 update reported more than 30,000 people in these teams, including contractors and partner-company reviewers.
evidence: The September 28 press-call transcript records the staffing target.
Facebook's December 4, 2018 update reports safety and security staffing above 30,000. The measure includes employees, contractors and partner-company staff, not only payroll headcount.

role: Founder of Amazon and Blue Origin
promise: Land humans on the Moon by 2024 with the Blue Moon lander
description: At the Blue Moon unveiling, Bezos said 'we can go to the Moon by 2024' and framed it as his generation's challenge. No Blue Origin crewed Moon landing occurred by the deadline; the uncrewed Blue Moon Mk1 lander had not even flown as of 2026.
evidence: No Blue Origin lunar mission flown by end of 2024
Blue Moon Mk1 first launch slipped to 2026 and beyond

review.note: May 9 presentation described Blue Moon helping NASA's 2024 goal, not necessarily an unconditional independent crewed-landing pledge. Need precise conditional wording and current Mk1 launch evidence; absence of a 2024 flight does not verify 'not even flown as of 2026'.

promise: Make India open-defecation free by October 2, 2019 (Gandhi's 150th birth anniversary)
description: Modi launched the sanitation campaign on October 2, 2014. He declared the open-defecation-free goal achieved in October 2019, but contemporary reporting questioned that claim.
evidence: The research article supports the launch and target dates.
Al Jazeera reports both the government's declaration and challenges to it.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the checked coverage does not reconcile the declaration with population-level survey evidence.
sources: Journal of Family Medicine and Primary Care

role: Leader of the Liberal Party of Canada
promise: "We are committed to ensuring that 2015 will be the last federal election conducted under the first-past-the-post electoral system."
description: Campaign pledge to replace first-past-the-post with a new voting system in time for the 2019 election. An all-party parliamentary committee reported in Dec 2016, and on Feb 1, 2017 Democratic Institutions Minister Karina Gould announced the government was abandoning reform because there was no consensus. The 2019 and 2021 elections were both held under first-past-the-post.
evidence: Liberal Party 2015 platform language on electoral reform
Feb 1, 2017 minister announcement that the promise would not be kept
2019 federal election conducted under FPTP

review.note: Pledge dates to June 16, 2015; October 19 is election day. Abandonment reported February 1, 2017.

promise: "We will legalize, regulate and restrict access to marijuana."
description: Campaign pledge to legalize recreational cannabis. The Cannabis Act received royal assent in June 2018 and legalization took effect October 17, 2018, roughly on the timeline promised.
evidence: Cannabis Act legalization effective Oct 17, 2018
Task force on cannabis legalization reported Dec 2016, government followed its recommendations

review.note: Government records confirm royal assent June 21 and effective October 17, 2018. Campaign date October 19, 2015 and treating later implementation date as an original deadline are not established.

promise: Budget 2021 targeted average regulated child-care fees of C$10 per day for children under six by fiscal 2025-26.
description: The April 19, 2021 budget proposed a Canada-wide early-learning and child-care plan, implemented through agreements with provinces and territories.
evidence: The federal budget notice supports the announcement and average-fee target.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the checked budget sources do not establish the comparable national average at fiscal year-end.

promise: Make India a $5 trillion economy by financial year 2024-25
description: Announced in his 2019 Independence Day address and repeated through 2019, promising India would be a $5 trillion economy by 2024-25. India's nominal GDP was about $3.6 trillion in FY2023-24 and about $4.3 trillion in FY2024-25 — well short of $5 trillion at the target date (only surpassed ~$4 trillion territory in 2025).
evidence: India nominal GDP ~$3.6T (FY2023-24) vs $5T target
IMF and government estimates put FY2024-25 GDP near $4.3T
2019 Independence Day speech set the $5T target

review.note: Official 2019 target is FY2024-25, which ends March 31, 2025, not 2024. August 15 quotation and dollar GDP outcomes still need contemporaneous speech and a consistent fiscal-year series.

promise: Double farmers' income by 2022.
description: Modi announced the aim of doubling farmers' income by 2022 at Bareilly on February 28, 2016.
evidence: The parliamentary record identifies the announcement and target.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the checked material does not establish a comparable national income baseline and deadline-year result.

promise: Putin's May 7, 2018 decree targeted Russia becoming one of the five largest economies by purchasing-power-parity GDP by 2024.
description: The target concerned the size of the economy measured at purchasing power parity, not nominal US-dollar GDP.
evidence: World Bank analysis identifies the national target and PPP comparison.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the checked reports do not provide the comparable 2024 ranking.

promise: Raise average life expectancy in Russia to 78 years by 2024.
description: Also from the May 2018 national-goals decree. Russian life expectancy fell to about 70 in 2020-21 due to COVID excess deaths, recovered to roughly 73.2 by 2024 — well below the 78 target.
evidence: Decree No. 204 set life expectancy of 78 by 2024
Rosstat data showed life expectancy ~73.2 in 2024

review.note: Retrieved government material distinguishes healthy life expectancy (67) from life expectancy and later resets 78 to 2030. Need original decree's 2024 metric and Rosstat's actual 2024 result; ~73.2 cannot be verified from these records.

role: General Secretary of the Communist Party of China and President of China
promise: Hu's report targeted doubling 2010 GDP and the per-capita income of urban and rural residents by 2020.
description: Hu Jintao's November 8, 2012 report to the 18th Party Congress set a target of doubling 2010 GDP and urban and rural residents' per-capita income by 2020.
evidence: The official report supports Hu's attribution and both parts of the target.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: comparable constant-price GDP and urban/rural income results were not established by the checked sources.

promise: "I would eliminate the $19 trillion national debt in eight years."
description: Made during a March 2016 campaign interview, claiming he could get rid of the debt in eight years, partly through growth and trade deals. The national debt instead rose from about $19.9 trillion when he took office to about $27.8 trillion when he left, and to roughly $34 trillion by early 2024.
evidence: US national debt ~$19.9T (Jan 2017) rising to ~$27.8T (Jan 2021) and ~$34T by 2024
Treasury debt-to-GDP data contradict the elimination claim

review.note: Interview was March 31, 2016, not March 1. Eight years meant presidential tenure; the March 2024 deadline is ungrounded. Treasury totals require separate verification.

promise: "I will build a great, great wall on our southern border, and I will make Mexico pay for that wall."
description: Trump promised a southern-border wall paid for by Mexico. Construction was funded by the United States. CRS reports 458 miles of wall panels installed during his administration, much of it replacing existing barriers.
evidence: CRS reports 458 miles installed by the end of the administration.
FactCheck.org reports $15 billion secured from US funding sources, not Mexican payment.

review.note: 458 miles is Trump-era installed panels, not all barriers existing at term end. $15 billion was total secured from several sources, not all diverted Pentagon funds. Original quotation/UTC date still require announcement transcript.

promise: Cancel $10,000 of federal student loan debt per borrower ($20,000 for Pell Grant recipients).
description: Campaign pledge to cancel $10,000 in student debt, delivered via executive action announced August 24, 2022 with discharges intended before January 2023. The Supreme Court struck it down in Biden v. Nebraska (June 30, 2023, 6-3), and no mass cancellation occurred.
evidence: Aug 24, 2022 White House announcement of $10k/$20k cancellation
SCOTUS ruling in Biden v. Nebraska (June 30, 2023) blocked the program
Debt forgiveness never discharged before the ruling

review.note: Supreme Court ruling supports failure of the 2022 plan. Current wording combines 2020 campaign relief with later Pell-specific $20,000 terms. October 15 and year-end 2022 original deadline are not established; eligibility/income limits omitted.

role: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom
promise: "50,000 more nurses" in the NHS.
description: The manifesto target of 50,000 additional nurses in the English NHS by 2024 was achieved by September 2023 on the government's full-time-equivalent measure. Nuffield noted unusually strong growth and dependence on overseas recruitment.
evidence: Nuffield Trust states the 50,000-nurse manifesto pledge was achieved.

review.note: Dataset reverses the conclusion of its named source. Nuffield says 50,000 increase achieved by September 2023. Measure is full-time-equivalent English NHS nurses including general practice, excluding health visitors; it is not all UK NHS.

promise: The Seine will be swimmable for the 2024 Paris Olympics, and "we will swim in it" (I will swim in the Seine in 2024).
description: Following a 2018 EUR1.4B cleanup plan, Macron repeatedly pledged in 2023-2024 that the Seine would host Olympic swimming and that he would personally swim in it. His planned July 31, 2024 swim was cancelled, the men's triathlon was postponed a day over water quality, and several athletes fell ill — but the triathlons and marathon swimming were ultimately held in the river, and the Seine reopened to public swimming in 2025.
evidence: Macron's planned July 2024 Seine swim was cancelled
Men's triathlon postponed due to bacterial contamination (July 30, 2024)
Marathon swimming events took place in the Seine in August 2024; river reopened to swimmers July 2025

review.note: Reported presidential swim had no fixed date, so July 31 cancellation and an Olympic-closing deadline are unsubstantiated. Training cancellations are not cancellation of the competitions. Need separate evidence for Macron personally, Olympic events and 2025 public opening; illness causation must not be implied.

promise: "Tesla will be feature complete for Full Self-Driving by the end of this year."
description: Tweeted in August 2019, part of a long series of FSD deadline promises (2019, 2020, 2021, 2024...). Full Self-Driving remained an incomplete beta in 2024-2025, requiring driver supervision and lacking regulatory certification — it was nowhere near feature-complete or autonomous by end of 2019.
evidence: FSD remained a supervised beta system through 2025
Musk's own later statements pushed deadlines to 2020 and beyond
No driverless/robotaxi FSD deployment existed by end of 2019

review.note: Search locates February podcast and October call, not the alleged August 16 tweet. 'Feature complete' was distinguished from unsupervised/regulator-approved driving; failure cannot be established solely by continued supervision.

promise: "We are going to land Starships on Mars as early as 2024."
description: Tweeted in October 2020, when Starship was still flying low-altitude hops. By the end of 2024 no Starship had reached orbit with a successful landing, let alone landed on Mars; the first uncrewed Mars landing is now targeted for the late 2020s, and the date was later revised to 2026 and beyond.
evidence: No Starship had landed on Mars by end of 2024
First orbital Starship flight only occurred April 2023 (exploded before separation)
SpaceX later revised Mars landing targets to the late 2020s

review.note: Mars Society confirms an October 16 appearance, not the purported tweet or exact quotation. 'As early as' is not a guaranteed latest deadline. April 2023 was an attempted orbital test, not successful orbit; 2024 flight outcomes and latest Mars schedule need mission records.

promise: Libra cryptocurrency would launch in 2020 (subject to US regulatory approval).
description: In congressional testimony on October 23, 2019, Zuckerberg committed to a 2020 launch window for the Libra stablecoin announced June 18, 2019. Regulatory pushback never cleared, the project was rebranded Diem in December 2020, and the Diem Association shut down in January 2022, selling assets to Silvergate.
evidence: Zuckerberg's Oct 23, 2019 House testimony naming 2020 as launch target
Libra rebranded Diem in Dec 2020 after regulators balked
Diem Association wound down Jan 2022 and sold to Silvergate

review.note: Congressional record confirms regulatory approval condition. Does not establish Zuckerberg gave an unconditional 2020 launch deadline in testimony. Need original launch plan and Diem sale announcement to check dissolution date/outcome.

role: Founder and CEO of Blue Origin
promise: New Glenn rocket's inaugural flight "no earlier than 2020."
description: At the September 2016 unveiling, Blue Origin and Bezos set the orbital rocket's first launch for 2020 (reaffirmed through 2017-2019 as the target slipped). The first New Glenn launch did not occur until January 16, 2025 — five years late, and its booster was lost on reentry.
evidence: Sept 12, 2016 announcement of inaugural flight "no earlier than 2020"
First launch (NG-1) occurred Jan 16, 2025
Repeated launch delays in 2021-2024 (ULA-78 launch slot disputes etc.)

review.note: Primary mission release confirms January 16, 2025 first launch and orbit. 'No earlier than 2020' is an earliest date, not a deadline; cannot score broken from that wording. Original announcement and alleged ULA-78 disputes unverified.

promise: Match all electricity used in Amazon's operations with renewable energy by 2025
description: Amazon reported in July 2024 that its 2023 operational electricity consumption was matched with renewable energy procurement. This is annual electricity matching, not elimination of all fossil-fuel use.
evidence: Amazon's July 10, 2024 release reports 100% electricity matching for 2023.

review.note: Achievement announcement was July 2024 about 2023 consumption. Matching annual electricity is not powering all operations exclusively with renewables. Original accelerated 2025 commitment's July 1 date still unverified.

promise: "We expect to complete the transition" of all Macs to Apple Silicon "in about two years."
description: Apple announced a transition expected to take about two years on June 22, 2020. The Apple-silicon Mac Pro became available June 13, 2023, which Apple identified as completion.
evidence: Apple's June 13, 2023 update says Mac Pro completes the transition.

review.note: Apple promised about two years, not a strict June 22 deadline. Primary completion record is June 2023, not 2022. June 2020 announced the transition, not M1 itself.

promise: "We believe that, in 2025, we may see the first AI agents 'join the workforce' and materially change the output of companies."
description: Written in Altman's "Reflections" blog post in January 2025. During 2025 OpenAI shipped Operator, Deep Research, ChatGPT agent payments and Codex, and enterprises began deploying agents — but agents' workforce integration remained largely assistive and limited, not the material, autonomous workforce transformation predicted.
evidence: OpenAI launched Operator (Jan 2025), Deep Research (Feb 2025), agent payments (Mar 2025)
2025 enterprise adoption of agents grew rapidly but remained supervised/limited
Altman's own 2025 statements characterized agents as a decade-scale transition

review.note: Original personal blog supports conditional 'may see', not a guaranteed autonomous-workforce transformation. January 10 publication date, March agent-payments launch and qualitative partial rating lack evidence. Product releases cannot establish or refute an undefined material-output forecast.

promise: Achieve the 20 Aichi Biodiversity Targets by 2020.
description: Adopted at COP 10 in Nagoya, October 2010, as a 20-target plan to 2020 covering habitat protection, species loss, pollution and sustainable use. The 2020 Global Biodiversity Outlook 5 reported that most targets were not met (and none fully achieved in the world at large), with biodiversity declining faster than ever.
evidence: Global Biodiversity Outlook 5 (2020) found most Aichi targets missed
Zero of 20 targets fully achieved at the global level per CBD
2024 study found countries failed to meet the targets due to weak implementation and funding

review.note: CBD supports adoption at COP10 and none of 20 fully achieved globally, with six partially achieved. Individual targets had different interim dates; exact adoption UTC date and unidentified 2024 study/causal claims still need evidence.

promise: Energy prices will come down 50% or more within a year
description: Trump's campaign pledge was to cut energy costs by half in his first year. PolitiFact found gasoline declined from $3.11 at inauguration to $2.78 in the second week of January 2026, while electricity and natural-gas prices rose.
evidence: January 2026 prices did not demonstrate a 50% reduction in energy costs.

review.note: PolitiFact supports missed first-year target but gives $2.78 gasoline in January 2026, contradicting claim it stayed $3.10-3.30. January 20 pledge date not established; promise originated during campaign.

promise: No tax on tips, overtime, or Social Security benefits
description: Campaign pledge to end taxes on tips, overtime pay and Social Security income. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (signed July 4, 2025) delivered only temporary tax deductions for tips, overtime and auto loans, all expiring in 2028; the Social Security tax exemption was never included, so the promise was only partially fulfilled.
evidence: OBBBA creates deductions for tips/overtime/auto loans rather than full exemptions (per Wikipedia, Second presidency of Donald Trump)
Deductions expire in 2028; no Social Security exemption was enacted
sources: Wikipedia: Second presidency of Donald Trump
Reuters coverage of One Big Beautiful Bill Act

review.note: IRS confirms separate deductions, not blanket exemption. A bundled June 15 announcement and July 4 deadline are not sourced; tips, overtime and Social Security pledges need individual dates. Inspect statutory eligibility, caps, expiry and Social Security treatment before certifying full narrative.

promise: I'm going to go to Fort Knox and check the gold
description: At his first cabinet meeting Trump said he would visit Fort Knox to verify US gold reserves, and Elon Musk offered to livestream an audit. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confirmed in July 2026 that the gold is 'present and accounted for', based on an audit dated September 2024 and a visit by the US Treasurer, but Trump had not personally visited Fort Knox by the deadline and the livestreamed audit never happened.
evidence: Bessent confirmed all gold reserves 'present and accounted for' (July 2026, based on a September 2024 audit)
Trump said in July 2026 that Musk would inspect Fort Knox; no confirmed personal visit by Trump

review.note: Reporting supports proposed visit, existing audits and Treasury assurance; no source establishes July 31, 2026 as a promised deadline. Another official's visit is not partial fulfillment of Trump's personal visit. February 26 exact quote and livestream commitment remain unverified.

promise: We're taking it back (the Panama Canal)
description: Trump called for taking back the Panama Canal. Separately, CK Hutchison announced a proposed ports transaction with a consortium including BlackRock, Global Infrastructure Partners and Terminal Investment. The proposed port sale is not transfer of the canal itself.
evidence: Reuters described an agreed ports sale still subject to compliance requirements in May 2025.
sources: Wikipedia: Second presidency of Donald Trump

review.note: Reuters describes a proposed sale, not proof of completed June transfer. Named consortium is BlackRock, GIP and Terminal Investment, not Bezos. Canal ownership is distinct from port concessions; deadline and final deal outcome still need checking.

promise: We're going to build an Iron Dome for America
description: Promised in his inaugural address and enacted via Executive Order 14186 of 27 January 2025, calling for a next-generation missile defense shield. The program (Golden Dome) advanced through DoD planning and interceptor demonstration contracts, and the FY2026 NDAA required annual reporting, but no operational nationwide shield existed by the July 2026 deadline; cost estimates reached $175-185 billion with delivery projected into the 2030s.
evidence: Executive Order 14186 signed January 27, 2025
FY2026 NDAA requires annual Golden Dome reports; system not operational as of July 2026

INDEC poverty figures peaked above 40% during his term (2020 readings for 2019-2020)

description: Apple announced on July 21, 2020 a plan for carbon neutrality across its business, manufacturing supply chain and product life cycle by 2030. Its plan combined a 75% emissions reduction with carbon removal for the remainder.
evidence: Apple's July 21, 2020 release supports the lifecycle goal and its reduction/removal approach.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the 2030 target remains future; the announcement is not proof of completion.

promise: Meta announced Quest 3 availability for October 10, 2023, starting at US$499.99 for 128GB.
description: Meta's September 27 announcement specified an October 10, 2023 release, starting at US$499.99 for 128GB. Subsequent reporting confirms the headset launched on that date.
evidence: Meta's Connect announcement establishes the October 10 target and the base-model price.
Android Central's retrospective availability account confirms the October 10, 2023 launch. This rates product availability, not delivery of every individual pre-order.

promise: Meta AI is on track to be the most used AI assistant in the world by the end of the year
description: Meta's claimed monthly active users and ChatGPT's weekly active users are not directly comparable. ChatGPT's 700-million-weekly-user milestone was reported in August 2025, not December 2024.
evidence: December 2024 ChatGPT reporting put weekly users at about 300 million.
700 million weekly users was reported in August 2025.

review.note: 700m weekly ChatGPT users was an August 2025 milestone, not December 2024. Monthly and weekly measures cannot adjudicate 'most used' without aligned definitions; partial status remains unproven.

promise: FTX is fine. Assets are fine.
description: The SEC complaint places Bankman-Fried's assurance about FTX assets on or about November 7, 2022 and alleges that customer assets had been diverted to Alameda.
evidence: SEC alleges the assurance was made while Bankman-Fried knew customer assets had been used by Alameda.

review.note: SEC complaint dates tweet on or about November 7, not November 8; remove exact 72-hour narrative. This is a present-tense assurance, not a dated future promise. Insolvency narrative and later convictions require separate judicial outcome source.

promise: Dimon warned that the US could enter a recession in six to nine months.
description: Dimon's October 10, 2022 warning was conditional. The recorded date is the outer edge of his forecast window, not a guaranteed event date.
evidence: Reuters supports the conditional warning and its date.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the checked material does not provide the matching NBER chronology for the forecast window.

promise: Moderna forecast production of between 700 million and one billion COVID-19 vaccine doses in 2021.
description: Moderna forecast production of 700 million to one billion vaccine doses for 2021. A WIPO case record states that it manufactured and shipped about 800 million doses in 2021, within that range; one billion was not a promised minimum.
evidence: The FY2020 filing establishes the production forecast range.
WIPO case D2022-2125 records approximately 800 million doses manufactured and shipped during 2021, supplying production-specific evidence in addition to Moderna's shipment reporting.

promise: We will manufacture 2.5 billion doses of the COVID-19 vaccine in 2021
description: Pfizer and BioNTech forecast at least 2.5 billion doses manufactured by end-2021. BioNTech subsequently reported more than 3.1 billion doses delivered by early March 2022; that is not a 2021 production total.
evidence: Company release distinguishes manufacturing forecast from cumulative deliveries through March 2022.

review.note: 3.1bn delivery figure is early March 2022, not end-2021. Forecast in company release is conditional. Original March 30/Bourla attribution and 2021 manufactured count need original results; remove 'rare mega-pledge' commentary.

promise: Hyperinflation is going to happen soon in the US and the world, and it will hit the poorest hardest
description: Dorsey tweeted that hyperinflation would hit the US and the world 'soon'. US inflation instead peaked at 9.1% in June 2022 (the highest in 40 years but nowhere near hyperinflation) and fell to roughly 3% by mid-2023. No hyperinflation occurred in the US or globally, and Bitcoin — which Dorsey linked to inflation hedging — fell about 75% from its Nov 2021 peak across 2022.
evidence: Tweet on @jack, April 2, 2022
US CPI peaked at 9.1% (June 2022) then declined to ~3% by mid-2023 — no hyperinflation
Global inflation also normalized through 2023

review.note: Contemporaneous coverage places hyperinflation tweets in October 2021, not April 2022. Need actual tweet timestamp for UTC and supplied tweet's contents. 'Soon' gives no year-end deadline; global claim and Bitcoin performance are peripheral and unverified.

promise: We expect to regain process leadership by 2025
description: At the 'Intel Unleashed' IDM 2.0 event, Gelsinger promised a 5-nodes-in-4-years roadmap (Intel 7/4/3/20A/18A) that would restore Intel's chipmaking lead over TSMC by 2025. Intel 18A was delayed from H2 2024 to 2025, TSMC's N2 kept the process lead, and Gelsinger was ousted as CEO in December 2024 before the goal was reached; Intel's first 18A product (Panther Lake) only shipped in late 2025. Process leadership was not regained in the promised window.
evidence: IDM 2.0 announced March 23, 2021 with 'regain process leadership' from TSMC as the goal
Intel delayed 18A (originally 2024 target) into 2025
Gelsinger removed as CEO December 2, 2024
TSMC (N2, 2025) retained the process lead; Panther Lake (18A) shipped late 2025

review.note: Intel primary records reaffirm 2025 process-leadership goal, but no original March 23 source for five-nodes roadmap was retrieved. Process leadership needs an explicit performance/power/density measure; cannot simply declare TSMC the winner from node names or CEO exit.

promise: Tesla Semi truck to enter production and start deliveries in 2019
description: Tesla first delivered Semi trucks to PepsiCo on December 1, 2022, after an initial 2019 production target.
evidence: Reuters reports the initial 2019 target and first deliveries in December 2022.

review.note: Reuters supports 2019 production target and first December 1, 2022 deliveries: delayed fulfillment. June 30 predates November unveiling. Local evening reveal/delivery timestamps require UTC checking before exact date replacement.

promise: New Tesla Roadster supercar (unveiled Nov 2017) to start production in 2020
description: The Roadster announced in November 2017 did not enter production by its 2020 target. September 2026 reporting still described a forthcoming reveal.
evidence: September 2026 coverage describes the product as six years beyond its original production target.

review.note: Current reporting supports delay beyond 2020 and planned 2026 reveal, not an exact count of eight postponements. June 30 predates November 2017 announcement; exact UTC date unresolved.

promise: Solar Roof tiles (unveiled Oct 28, 2016) to begin installations by summer 2017
description: Tesla reported initial Solar Roof installations on employee homes in August 2017. These preceded broader customer availability.
evidence: August 2017 reports confirm employee-home installations.

review.note: Employee installations already existed in August 2017. Whether pledge required general customers remains unresolved; original June date and December deadline conflict with stated unveiling/summer timing.

promise: Battery Day (Sept 22, 2020): 4680 cells in volume production by end of 2021, and a $25,000 Tesla car 'in about 3 years'
description: 4680 volume production only ramped in 2023-2024; the ~$25,000 car never shipped — Reuters reported in April 2024 that Tesla scrapped its low-cost car plans.
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: Tesla confirms Battery Day on September 22, not June 30. Combined record has two different milestones/deadlines and needs splitting; $25,000-in-three-years does not mature in 2021. Exact 4680 volume commitment/outcome remains unverified.

promise: 'No advertising coming onto Netflix. Period.' (June 2015)
description: Netflix later reversed its no-third-party-advertising stance by launching an advertising-supported plan, including US availability from November 3, 2022.
evidence: Netflix's launch announcement confirms advertising-supported service in November 2022.

review.note: Contemporaneous no-ad report was June 1, not June 30. Netflix confirms US ad tier November 3, 2022 (Canada November 1). No explicit 2022 deadline for indefinite stance was established.

promise: Pledge of $250 million to compensate hosts for COVID-19 cancellations (March 30, 2020)
description: Airbnb's March 30, 2020 host letter pledged $250 million for qualifying COVID-19 cancellations, paying 25% of what hosts would receive under their cancellation policies.
evidence: Host letter announces funding and eligibility; it is not a final disbursement report.

review.note: Primary host letter is March 30. Eligibility concerns reservation check-in dates and bookings before March 14, not cancellation dates alone. Announcement does not establish all $250m paid; kept and year-end deadline remain unverified.

promise: Uber would become profitable by 2021 (Q3 2019 shareholder letter)
description: Uber reported its first positive adjusted-EBITDA quarter as a public company in Q3 2021, at $8 million. This is a non-GAAP measure, not net profit.
evidence: November 4, 2021 earnings release identifies Q3 as the first positive adjusted-EBITDA quarter.

review.note: Q3 2019 results were November 4, not June 30. First positive adjusted EBITDA quarter was Q3 2021, not Q4. Adjusted EBITDA is not GAAP profitability; original target wording still needs call transcript.

promise: Aim for all Uber journeys in London to use fully electric cars by 2025
description: Uber's October 23, 2018 Clean Air Plan set a 2025 all-electric London-journey goal and introduced a per-mile fee to help drivers switch vehicles.
evidence: Uber's dated Clean Air Plan sets the all-electric London-journey goal.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the checked plan does not provide a comparable share of London journeys at the end of 2025.

promise: Expect non-music content to account for more than 20% of Spotify listening over time
description: Daniel Ek's February 6, 2019 Audio-First essay forecast that more than 20% of Spotify listening would eventually be non-music. It did not specify a deadline.
evidence: Original essay uses an open-ended forecast, not a 2020 target.

review.note: Original February 6 forecast says 'over time', not by 2020. No primary listening-hours figure supports the quarter-of-listening outcome; user participation in podcasts is not share of listening.

promise: Spectacles (Nov 2016) would launch Snap's hardware era as a 'camera company' product — expected to sell well
description: Only ~150,000 pairs sold by Oct 2017 (~$8M revenue); Snap took a ~$40M inventory write-down and later admitted Spectacles was the 'wrong decision'.
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: Sources substantiate sales/write-down, but no measurable promise, June 30 announcement or year-end sales deadline was found. 'Expected to sell well' is not an attributable commitment. $8m revenue and 'wrong decision' scope require original financials/interview.

promise: Square would build a bitcoin hardware wallet and service to make bitcoin custody 'more mainstream' (July 2021)
description: Block launched the Bitkey self-custody hardware wallet in Dec 2023, fulfilling the promise (two years after the announcement).
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: Block's actual launch page located; announcement versus preorders versus hardware shipment must be separated. June 30 predates the described July commitment; December 2023 original deadline not established. Current existence does not certify on-time delivery.

promise: Salesforce's analyst-day presentation targeted $20-22 billion in annual revenue for fiscal 2022.
description: Salesforce presented the target in November 2017. It reported $26.49 billion for fiscal 2022, ending January 31, 2022, above the numerical target range.
evidence: The analyst-day deck dates the forecast and gives the $20-22 billion range.
The FY2022 release reports $26.49 billion.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21 on a like-for-like basis: the checked figures do not reconcile the original organic-growth and accounting assumptions with later reported revenue.

promise: GM planned at least 20 new all-electric models globally by 2023.
description: GM reiterated the global model-launch target in its June 12, 2018 sustainability announcement.
evidence: GM's dated announcement supports the target and global scope.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: a complete global model inventory, including China and joint ventures, was not established.

promise: Cruise robotaxi unit to generate $1 billion in annual revenue by 2025
description: GM announced on December 10, 2024 that it would stop funding Cruise robotaxi development and combine technical work with its personal-vehicle autonomy programme. This was a refocusing and restructuring decision, not evidence of immediate legal closure.
evidence: GM's December 10 announcement distinguishes robotaxi funding cessation from integration of technical teams.

review.note: GM announced stopping robotaxi funding and integrating teams, not immediate dissolution of Cruise. Exact original speaker/date and revenue/loss totals still require primary records.

promise: Ford to be producing 600,000 EVs annually by the end of 2023, and 2 million by 2026 (Ford+ event, May 26, 2021)
description: Ford sold only ~110,000 EVs globally in 2023; Farley pushed the 600K milestone to 2024 and delayed the 2 million-by-2026 goal indefinitely.
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: Ford sources specify annualized production run rate, not actual yearly sales. June 30/May 26 original attribution needs verification; 110,000 sales cannot test run rate. Need dated delay announcement and actual run rate, with separate 2026 milestone.

promise: NVIDIA's $40 billion acquisition of Arm (announced Sept 2020) expected to close by early 2022
description: NVIDIA and SoftBank terminated the proposed Arm acquisition in February 2022 because of regulatory challenges. Their agreement had been announced in September 2020.
evidence: NVIDIA's termination release confirms the transaction did not close.

review.note: NVIDIA confirms September 13, 2020 announcement, not June 30, and termination in February 2022. Newsroom February 7 versus earnings February 8 likely needs UTC reconciliation. Early-2022 expectation does not justify December deadline; remove unsupported superlative.

promise: Apple's services business would grow to the size of a Fortune 100 company (July 2016; reiterated in Jan 2017 with a 2020 timeframe)
description: Services revenue hit $53.8 billion in FY2020 — larger than the typical Fortune 100 company's annual revenue.
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: 2016 Fortune-100 forecast referred to next fiscal year, not 2020. Likely conflates it with a later services-doubling target. Original date, exact scope, Fortune-100 revenue threshold and outcome require earnings transcripts; 'typical' is not the cutoff.

promise: Self-driving 'Apple Car' to launch around 2025 (reported internal target, Bloomberg, Dec 2020)
description: Apple canceled its electric car project in February 2024 after a decade of effort, with team members reassigned to AI work.
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: Bloomberg supports internal cancellation in February 2024, not a public Tim Cook commitment. June 30 2020 and alleged reported launch target remain unestablished; an anonymously reported internal schedule should not become a direct CEO quote.

promise: 'We want to get a billion people in virtual reality' (Oculus Connect 5, Oct 2017)
description: Zuckerberg announced a goal of bringing one billion people into VR at Oculus Connect 4 in October 2017. Contemporary reporting explicitly said no deadline was set.
evidence: WIRED reports the billion-person goal had no deadline.

review.note: Goal announced October 11, 2017 at Connect 4, without a deadline. June 30, Connect 5 and 2025 due date are unsupported. Active headset estimates are not equivalent to people who ever used VR.

promise: Facebook would not take a cut of creators' revenue until at least 2023 (June 7, 2021)
description: Facebook said on June 7, 2021 that specified creator tools, including paid online events and fan subscriptions, would remain free until 2023. This was not a blanket promise covering every form of creator revenue.
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: June 7 primary update specifies selected monetization tools and 'until 2023', not necessarily all creator revenues through December 2023. Later extension/outcome needs evidence.

promise: Disney targeted 60-90 million Disney+ subscribers by the end of fiscal 2024.
description: Disney's April 11, 2019 forecast was exceeded numerically: fiscal-2024 results reported 122.7 million Disney+ Core subscribers and 35.9 million Hotstar subscribers.
evidence: The investor-day material gives the 60-90 million fiscal-2024 target.
Official results give the September 28, 2024 period end and separate Core and Hotstar counts.

promise: Combined streaming business (Disney+) would break even by the end of fiscal 2024 (pledge after Iger's return, late 2022)
description: Disney reported its combined streaming businesses became profitable in fiscal Q3 2024, one quarter ahead of its fiscal-Q4 guidance. This combines Entertainment DTC with ESPN+.
evidence: Disney Q3 earnings release reports first combined streaming profitability ahead of guidance.

review.note: Combined streaming first profitable in fiscal Q3 2024, ahead of Q4 guidance. Distinguish combined non-GAAP streaming result from Entertainment DTC or Disney+ alone. June 2022 attribution conflicts with Iger's later return; exact pledge/fiscal deadline need checking.

promise: Merger with Discovery would generate $3 billion in annual cost synergies (2022)
description: WBD achieved the $3 billion run-rate target and later raised it to more than $5 billion.
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: SEC filings confirm merger and restructuring programmes, but retrieved passages do not establish June 30 promise, 2024 deadline or realized $3bn/$5bn annual run-rate synergies. Restructuring charges are not savings; raised target is not fulfillment.

promise: Harry Potter: Wizards Unite (announced Nov 2017) to launch in 2018
description: Game launched June 21, 2019 (a year late) and was shut down in January 2022 after disappointing performance.
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: Niantic records April/May 2019 regional beta, demonstrating availability before purported June launch. Original November 2017/2018 target and exact public launch need sources. June 30 original date impossible for November announcement; 'one year late' overstates June versus December miss.

promise: Oculus Rift consumer headset would sell for 'around $350' (2014 statements)
description: Oculus announced a $599 consumer Rift price in January 2016; release followed on March 28. Luckey later acknowledged that his September 2015 price-range comments were poorly communicated.
evidence: Contemporary review distinguishes January pricing announcement from March 28 release.
Luckey's account places the ballpark statement in September 2015.

review.note: January 2016 was price/preorder announcement; consumer release was March 28. Luckey's acknowledged ballpark remark was September 2015 and included 'cost more', not a guaranteed $350 price. Exact original date still unresolved.

promise: Raise the child tax credit from $2,000 to $5,000 per child (Aug 2024 campaign pledge)
description: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (signed 4 Jul 2025) raised the credit only to $2,200, inflation-indexed, with the refundable portion unchanged — no $5,000 credit was ever enacted.
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: IRS source located for actual credit, but original Vance interview/date/deadline and full post-law parameters still need checking. January 2023 predates the described August 2024 proposal. Distinguish proposal/aspiration from guaranteed enacted amount.

promise: Victory Plan (presented 16 Oct 2024) demanded an immediate NATO membership invitation as point one, i.e., an invitation before the war's end
description: Zelenskyy presented the Victory Plan on October 16, 2024. Its first point requested an invitation to NATO; it was not a guarantee that Ukraine itself would issue or secure one by year-end.
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: Official presentation dated October 16, 2024, not January 2023. Invitation was a request to allies, not something Zelenskyy could issue; no December 31 promise established.

promise: Zelenskyy said the war could end in 2025 if implementation of his Victory Plan began immediately.
description: Presenting the Victory Plan to the European Council on October 17, 2024, Zelenskyy said the war could end by the next year if implementation began immediately. It was a conditional assessment.
evidence: The presidential account supports the date and immediate-implementation condition.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the checked presentation does not establish that the proposal's conditions were implemented.

promise: Total victory and destruction/elimination of Hamas — 'we will not stop the war before achieving all of its goals' (April 2024), vowing to continue 'until victory'
description: On April 30, 2024 Netanyahu said Israel would not halt the war before achieving its goals and would enter Rafah with or without a deal. The statement gave no calendar deadline.
evidence: April 30 reporting records continued-war and Rafah statements without a year-end deadline.

review.note: April 30, 2024 statement supports conditional continuation and Rafah goals, not January 2023 or a fixed year-end deadline. Precise Hamas status, geographic control and ceasefire claims need distinct evidence; remove unverified percentages.

promise: Bring all 251 hostages home
description: Reuters reported that the remains of Ran Gvili, described as the last Israeli hostage held in Gaza, were recovered on January 26, 2026. Returned hostages and returned remains must be distinguished.
evidence: January 26, 2026 reporting contradicts the claim that the last Israeli hostage remained unreturned in mid-2026.

review.note: January 2023 predates October 7 abductions and no December 2023 deadline is sourced. Reuters reports recovery of the last Israeli hostage's remains January 26, 2026, contradicting stale mid-2026 narrative. Alive versus remains, foreign hostages and all-251 scope need explicit reconciliation before status replacement.

promise: Pass 'Plan C' judicial reform — election of judges by popular vote — during her first months
description: President Lopez Obrador signed the judicial reform in September 2024 with President-elect Sheinbaum present, before she took office on October 1.
evidence: Contemporaneous reports attribute signing to Lopez Obrador, with Sheinbaum attending.

review.note: Reporting establishes AMLO signed the reform before Sheinbaum took office, not that she passed it during her first months. January 2023 pledge and first-month commitment need evidence; local September 15 evening can be September 16 UTC.

promise: Constitutional ban on re-election of any popularly elected office, promised to take effect in 2027
description: The anti-re-election rule was published 1 Apr 2025, but its implementation was postponed from 2027 to 2030.
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: Official April 1 decree confirms anti-reelection provisions apply from 2030 elections. Original January 2023/2027 promise, exact offices and role at announcement remain unestablished; do not describe every elected office as newly covered.

promise: Free nutritious meals (Makan Bergizi Gratis) for schoolchildren, pregnant women and toddlers — targeting 82.9 million beneficiaries
description: Indonesia launched the free-meals programme on January 6, 2025. Reuters reported 570,000 recipients on opening day and a plan then targeting 82.9 million beneficiaries by 2029.
evidence: Contemporaneous launch report distinguishes initial coverage from the 2029 full-scale target.

review.note: Launch reporting gives 82.9m by 2029, not original 2025 deadline. Later accelerated target requires its own dated announcement. Budget, poisoning and arrest allegations unverified; replace with launch facts.

promise: 8% annual economic growth by the end of his term (2029)
description: Prabowo advocated an 8% annual growth target before taking office in 2024. The record's stated 2029 deadline has not passed; lower interim growth does not establish failure at that deadline.
evidence: 2024 Reuters reports describe the growth ambition, not its eventual outcome.

review.note: Reuters supports an 8% growth ambition; current roughly 5% growth or forecasts cannot establish a missed 2029 deadline in 2026. Exact original date and end-term interpretation require source.

promise: Defeat inflation ('kill inflation', the overriding goal of his first year)
description: Annual inflation fell from 211.4% (2023) and 254.2% (first month) to 117.8% (2024) and ~31.8% by Sept 2025, with monthly inflation at a five-year low of 1.5% (June 2025) — a huge reduction, though inflation was not eliminated.
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: Search returned INDEC technical indexes, not the needed CPI tables or original pledge. Date/deadline conflict ('first year' versus 2027) unresolved. Need monthly-versus-annual series; claimed June 1.5% must not be certified from unrelated construction-price data.

promise: Reduce poverty
description: INDEC's survey of 31 urban agglomerations reported poverty of 41.7% in H2 2023, 52.9% in H1 2024 and 31.6% in H1 2025. Indigence fell from 18.1% in H1 2024 to 6.9% in H1 2025.
evidence: INDEC's H1 2025 report supplies a comparable half-year series for the same urban survey scope.

review.note: INDEC's consistent half-year series gives 31.6% poverty and 6.9% indigence in H1 2025, not 7.4%. Its H1 2024 poverty figure is 52.9%, not the separate 57.4% monthly estimate. Original promise/date/deadline and an outcome threshold remain unestablished.

promise: Campaign pledge (2023): dollarize the economy and abolish the central bank
description: In April 2025 Argentina relaxed specified foreign-exchange controls and introduced a moving ARS1,000-1,400 per dollar band. This retained the peso and central bank, but does not by itself establish permanent abandonment of dollarization.
evidence: BCRA lists measures relaxed and the peso-band regime; it does not describe universal removal of all controls.

review.note: BCRA describes April 2025 relaxation of specified controls and a currency band, not complete dismantling. Keeping peso then does not prove permanent abandonment of dollarization. Original date and 2025 deadline unverified.

promise: Unblock Poland's EU Recovery funds (KPO, ~€59.8bn) 'within weeks' of taking office
description: First tranche of PLN 27bn (~€6.3bn) arrived 15 Apr 2024 after the Commission's positive assessment of 29 Feb 2024; further payments followed through 2025, though the full €59.8bn had not all been disbursed.
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: Commission/Euronews support April 15, 2024 payment and financing total. January 2023 promise and 'within weeks' source absent; unblocking eligibility is not the same as first tranche payment. Near-duplicate of index 78 with conflicting outcome chronology.

promise: Liberalize the abortion law — legal abortion on request up to 12 weeks of pregnancy
description: The Sejm rejected a bill for partial decriminalization of abortion-related acts by 218 votes to 215. That bill should be distinguished from broader legislation establishing access to abortion on request.
evidence: Sejm's legislative record identifies the proposal as partial decriminalization and records the 215-218 vote.

review.note: Sejm record is partial decriminalization, not the same as comprehensive legal access on request. Original pledge date and deadline unverified; do not equate rejection of this bill with voting down every liberalization proposal.

promise: Create Great British Energy, a publicly owned energy company
description: Great British Energy Limited was incorporated on October 10, 2024. Its governance page records Royal Assent to the Great British Energy Act on May 15, 2025; company formation and legislation are distinct milestones.
evidence: GBE's governance page records incorporation in 2024, before the 2025 Act.

review.note: GBE's own governance page records incorporation October 10, 2024, separate from May 2025 legislation. This resolves the apparent 2024/2025 outcome contradiction, but original promise date/deadline still unsourced. Search text of statutory explanatory notes says April 15 while company says May 15; verify Act header before relying on explanatory-note date.

promise: Increase defence spending to 2.5% of GDP
description: Starmer announced on February 25, 2025 that defence spending would rise to 2.5% of GDP from April 2027, funded partly by reducing aid to 0.3% of GNI. The implementation date remains future.
evidence: Government announcement specifies April 2027; appropriations and plans are not proof of achieved expenditure.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the April 2027 implementation date remains future and the checked funding plan is not a spending outturn.

promise: Deliver 1.5 million new homes over the parliament via radical planning reform
description: The Planning and Infrastructure Act received Royal Assent on December 18, 2025 as part of the government's plan to build 1.5 million homes during Parliament. Enactment does not establish the number of completed homes.
evidence: Official announcement confirms enactment and links it to the housing target.

review.note: Royal Assent December 18 confirmed. Planning legislation is an enabling action, not houses delivered; remove unsupported pace assessment unless statistical source added. Original placeholder pledge date and precise end-Parliament deadline unverified.

promise: Zeitenwende (27 Feb 2022): €100bn Bundeswehr special fund and reaching NATO's 2% of GDP defence spending
description: Scholz announced a EUR100 billion Bundeswehr special fund and higher defence spending in his February 27, 2022 policy statement. Establishing the fund and spending its resources are distinct measures.
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: Speech is February 27, 2022, not January 2023. Creating special fund differs from drawing it down, and original spending pledge was sustained annual expenditure, not merely reaching it once. 2024/2025 percentages and drawdown require budget/NATO evidence.

promise: Pension reform raising the retirement age from 62 to 64
description: The 2023 pension-age reform was subsequently modified by the December 30, 2025 social-security financing law and May 2026 decrees. The age-64 schedule was shifted to the 1969 birth cohort rather than 1968.
evidence: Official parliamentary responses describe suspension provisions and their implementing decrees.

review.note: Parliamentary responses confirm 2025 legislation suspended/adjusted rollout and May 2026 implementing decrees. Existing claim that the 2023 schedule remained unchanged through 2026 is stale. Need original promise and enactment date; March 16 use of 49.3 is not final promulgation.

promise: Restore sound public finances / keep the deficit on a path toward the EU's 3% of GDP ceiling
description: The deficit was 5.8% of GDP in 2024 (up from 5.4% in 2023 and at risk of exceeding 6%), public debt reached 116.5% of GDP in 2025, and the 3% target is far out of reach.
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: Current Reuters reporting describes a 2029 deficit target, not 2027. Need original dated promise and explicit postponement to adjudicate abandonment; forecasts cannot alone establish a future deadline missed. Exact debt/deficit vintage and definitions remain unverified.

promise: Increase medical school admissions by 2,000 per year to fix the doctor shortage (announced 6 Feb 2024)
description: On April 17, 2025 the government announced that the 2026 medical-school quota would return to 3,058, the pre-expansion level.
evidence: Education ministry announcement and Yonhap coverage confirm the 2026 quota reversal on April 17, 2025.

review.note: Education ministry/ Yonhap confirm April 17, 2025 return to 3,058 for 2026. This is after the record's own April removal timing, so 'unravelled before removal' is not supported. Original February 6 announcement and exact 2025 increment need sources.

promise: Keep the federal carbon price as the cornerstone of climate policy
description: Canada ceased applying the federal consumer fuel charge from April 1, 2025 and removed the consumer-price requirement for provinces. This should not be described as repeal of every federal carbon-pricing mechanism.
evidence: Finance Canada's backgrounder specifies the consumer fuel charge and consumer-facing benchmark.

review.note: Official measure ceased consumer fuel charge, not all industrial carbon pricing. Original January 2023 promise/deadline not sourced. A successor's action must not be described as Trudeau's own implementation; March 14 was transition day, not weeks after departure.

promise: Cut immigration levels to ease housing and social pressures
description: Permanent-resident targets were cut from 500,000 to 395,000 (2025), 380,000 (2026) and 365,000 (2027), and the plans were implemented.
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: Official 2024 plan supports reduced future targets. January 2023 attribution and actual 2025 admissions are not established; publishing targets does not prove they were implemented. Later 2026-2027 plans could revise the figures.

promise: Present major European defence funding proposals within 100 days of her second Commission — delivered as ReArm Europe
description: The Commission's European Defence White Paper was issued on March 19, 2025 and provides the framework for ReArm Europe. The White Paper and financing-plan announcements are separate milestones.
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: White Paper is dated March 19, 2025 and distinguished from ReArm financing plan. Need original 100-day commitment/start point; January 2023 date cannot describe second Commission. Do not substitute an earlier funding announcement for a promised White Paper without checking scope.

promise: Allies must move to a 'wartime mindset' and raise defence spending far above 2% of GDP
description: NATO Allies adopted the Hague declaration on June 25, 2025, committing to 5% of GDP annually by 2035, including 3.5% core defence and up to 1.5% related investment. Adoption is not proof of immediate spending delivery.
evidence: NATO reports Allied adoption without a Spain signatory exception.

review.note: NATO records collective adoption, not 'all except Spain signed'. Spain disputed its spending obligation but that differs from not adopting declaration. Agreement to 2035 spending is not actual expenditure by 2025; original Rutte speech/date unverified.

promise: We are going to have a 48-team World Cup.

evidence: FIFA Council unanimously voted for a 48-team format on 2017-01-10
2026 World Cup in USA/Canada/Mexico ran with 48 teams as promised

review.note: FIFA confirms January 10, 2017 expansion decision and June 11, 2026 scheduled opener. Retrieved schedule is prospective, not evidence the tournament actually ran. Need actual competition report and exact Infantino quote before full certification.

promise: The labor reforms will be completed by the time of the 2022 World Cup (as reported).
description: Amnesty documented continuing gaps in remedy for World Cup workers. Its November 2024 response to FIFA's legacy fund said that fund did not provide the requested compensation for exploited workers.
evidence: Amnesty distinguished a FIFA legacy fund from a worker-compensation programme.

review.note: Amnesty's November 2024 account says FIFA legacy fund excluded compensation for exploited workers; the record's launched-2023 compensation-fund claim is unsupported. Original Al Thawadi quotation/date and full kafala abolition claim need primary legal/interview evidence.

promise: We want to study whether we can have a World Cup every two years (as reported).
description: FIFA's 2021 Congress requested a feasibility study of biennial World Cups. FIFA subsequently reported studies and consultations. This fulfills a study commitment, not a separate promise to adopt a biennial tournament.
evidence: FIFA's 2021 report documents the study request and resulting analysis.

review.note: Literal promise is to study feasibility. FIFA's annual report documents commissioned studies and consultations, so non-adoption does not make that study promise broken. Exact May 21 quotation and September 2022 deadline still need source.

promise: Paris 2024 will be the first Olympic Games with full gender parity on the field of play (as reported).
description: Paris 2024 allocated equal female and male athlete quota places. Equal planned quotas should not be described as proof that the actual number of competing athletes was exactly 5,250 women and 5,250 men.
evidence: IOC's progress report identifies quota places as the parity indicator.

review.note: IOC report measures equal quota places, not proof exactly 5,250 of each gender actually competed. Original March 8 date and actual field require official participation table.

promise: I think that will happen and I believe it will happen in the next five to ten years (London franchise, as reported).
description: Goodell repeatedly called an NFL franchise in London 'inevitable' with a five-to-ten-year window from 2017. By the midpoint (2022) and through 2026, no London franchise has been awarded; the league has held International Series games but expansion remains undecided.
evidence: Goodell's 2017 comments at NFL owners meetings called London franchise inevitable
No expansion franchise awarded as of mid-2026; London team still 'under consideration'

review.note: NFL source contains a conditional five-to-ten-year prediction, but 2017 date/exact wording not established. Even from 2017, upper endpoint is 2027, not October 2022; evaluating the midpoint as final deadline is invalid. Need original timestamp and current franchise evidence.

promise: We believe this will reduce average game time by roughly 25 minutes (pitch clock, as reported).

evidence: Pitch clock implemented from opening day 2023
Average game time dropped 24 minutes from 3:04 (2022) to 2:40 (2023)

review.note: MLB supports reduction in game time during 2023, but retrieved September report is not full-season final result. Exact Manfred quote, September 13 announcement and promised 25-minute metric are unestablished.

promise: CNN+ will be the next generation of CNN — a premium streaming subscription service for news (as reported).
description: CNN+ launched on March 29, 2022. Warner Bros. Discovery announced its closure on April 21; announcement and final service shutdown were different dates.
evidence: April 21 reporting described cessation as forthcoming, not already completed.

review.note: April 21 was shutdown announcement, not actual cessation. Original November 17 quote/deadline and final shutdown day need source; a pledge to launch differs from a promise of commercial longevity. CNN page also has an apparent 2021 dateline typo despite 2022 heading.

promise: We're targeting 150 million DTC subscribers by 2025 (as reported).

evidence: Investor Day guidance of 150M DTC subs by 2025 reported by Variety/CNBC
Paramount+ subscriber base stayed near 70M through 2024-2025

review.note: Contemporaneous report identifies a 100m-by-2024 target, not 150m-by-2025. Need primary investor transcript to confirm global/US scope because retrieved report's geography also needs corroboration. Paramount+ alone is not necessarily all DTC subscriptions.

evidence: Comcast Investor Day 2021 guidance of 30-35M Peacock subs by 2024
Peacock reported ~36M paid subscribers at end of 2024

review.note: Comcast SEC filing confirms 36m paid Peacock subscribers at end-2024. Original June 22 2021 event/quote and 30-35m paid versus active-account measure remain unsupported.

evidence: Disney's FY2024 results separate Core and Hotstar counts.

sources: Marvel Studios SDCC 2022 panel coverage, Variety
Variety / The Hollywood Reporter delay reports 2023-2025

Associated Press reported the completed opening weekend on July 13, 2025, rather than merely repeating a future release schedule.

evidence: Lucasfilm's announcement supports the project and Christmas 2023 target.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the checked announcement does not establish cancellation or actual release.

review.note: The December 10 announcement supports Christmas 2023, not an exact December 22 deadline. The asserted shelving and absence of all Star Wars films through 2025 require outcome evidence; publication remains withheld.

promise: Ad-free is a real part of the brand promise.

evidence: Hastings' Q3 2021 earnings call statement on ad-free brand promise
Netflix launched ad-supported tier 2022-11-03 and phased out ad-free basic plan in 2023

review.note: Search did not establish the alleged October 19, 2021 Hastings quotation. Netflix's primary launch notice supports a US advertising tier on November 3, 2022, but that launch date is not an original promise deadline. Do not infer a dated no-advertising guarantee from general brand rhetoric.

promise: UMG and Deezer announced plans to explore an artist- and fan-focused streaming model.
